notes: Sayer of the Bell (WORLD_BIBLE 1.1). Main-quest 3 gate: receives Wren's letter, delivers the first lecture, names the Circle's price. Her account fails on why gossip warms a village, and she knows it and has a defence.

greetings.text: You are the Warden's letter. I have read it twice. It is badly sealed and entirely to the point, which is Tallow all over.
You have heard all three now. Do not tell me which you preferred. It is forbidden, and I would be able to tell from your face, and then we should both be embarrassed.
You said a scraped name aloud in my lecture hall. I have not decided what I think. I have decided that it was correctly done.
You have been in the roll. Say nothing on the stair; say it in the tuning room, where the stone takes the sound.
The Circle has begun saying your name without meaning to. That is data, you understand. You are becoming a loud object.

greet.speaker: Aldith Sulion
greet.text: Sulion. Sayer of the Bell. Speak up; the stalk swallows a quiet voice and I will not pretend to have heard you.

choices.text: A letter, from Warden Tallow.
Give me your account of the Dwindling.
The others say you are wrong.
What does your account fail at?
What does the Circle want for a verdict?
Tell me about Saying.
Teach me one.
Who was Tessane?
Can I be taught?
That will do.

joining.speaker: Aldith Sulion
joining.text: Taught. — You have sat through my account and, I am told, through Cadwen's, and through whatever the clans call theirs, and you have not yet said which one you prefer. That is the entire qualification. The Circle takes Listeners: allowed to hear all three, forbidden to prefer one out loud. It is a low rank and it is the only honest one we have. — Take the stone. Read the First Lecture, which you will find tedious and which you will need. Then Say the Chalk Hound's name over the down until the down says it back to you; it will take longer than you expect and you will feel a fool, and both of those are the lesson. Then come and find what the Circle scraped off its own roll, and we will see what sort of Listener you are.

the_letter.speaker: Aldith Sulion
the_letter.text: 'To whichever of the Circle is speaking this week.' She has been waiting eleven years to write that sentence. — And a tine of Oroth stone from the crown of the Cracked Toll, humming a half-note under the bell. Do you know what you have in your hand? No. Good; the ones who arrive knowing are useless. The Circle will hear you. Three lectures, three Sayers, and you will attend all three and you will not say which you prefer.

lecture.speaker: Aldith Sulion
lecture.text: The world is the ringing of a bell struck once, before time. Sound is being. Where the ringing is loud there is warmth and colour; where it thins, things go still and unsaid, and the deep places are where it thinned first. This is not a metaphor and I will not have it taught as one. The Builders understood it better than we do: they raised the Harmonies to sustain the note, cathedral-machines the size of towns, and they failed, and their failure is the only honest engineering report we possess. — Your tine is a tuning fork. It is holding a note half a step under the bell. Two things that were made to agree have stopped agreeing. That is what is happening to the world, in your hand, small enough to carry.

the_others.speaker: Aldith Sulion
the_others.text: Cresswell will tell you the world is a candle and that gossip is a kind of prayer, and he will be charming, and you will want it to be true. Ask him to explain the Cantor's Seat, which is cold and enormous and has stood for a thousand years with nobody gossiping about it at all. He will say something warm and change the subject; he is very good at it and he knows that I know. — Ondrael will tell you something vast is breathing in. Ask her why the Seat has not gone, when it is the oldest and deepest thing in the basin and should have been the first mouthful. She will say she does not know. She is the most honest of us and it costs her.

the_failure.speaker: Aldith Sulion
the_failure.text: A fair question and the only one worth the fee. — My account cannot explain why a village that talks about itself stays warm. It should not matter. A hundred Vale farmers saying each other's names over a hedge is not sound in any sense I can measure; it is not loud, it is not sustained, it does not carry past the next field. And it works. I have measured villages. The ones that talk hold their colour. I have no account of it and I teach the Bell anyway, because an account that fails at one thing and predicts nine is worth more than a warm feeling that predicts nothing. Write that down if you write anything down.

the_price.speaker: Aldith Sulion
the_price.text: The Circle will pronounce in council, on the tine and the hum together, and the price is the bell from the altar of the Drowned Nave. We have wanted it for three hundred years. The reedfolk have never offered it and we have never taken it, which I would like noted as restraint. — You think this squalid. It is squalid. It is also the only way the council sits: three Sayers who disagree will not convene for a question, but they will convene for an object. Bring me the object and you will get your answer, and you will get it in triplicate and contradictory, which is the only honest form an answer has ever come in.

saying.speaker: Aldith Sulion
saying.text: Saying is speaking the world louder. Not commanding it; there are no commands. You attend to a thing very precisely, you name what it is, and you say it until it is more so than it was. A Listener may Say a name back off a chalk hill. A Sayer may Say a bridge. — The three-times rule you will have noticed me keeping: a new word is said three times before it is used in a sentence, so that the mouth is not carrying anything it has not weighed. Students find it comic for a month and then they do it for life.

tessane.speaker: Aldith Sulion
tessane.text: ...Say it in here. Thank you. — Tessane was a Sayer of this Circle, Y.T. 932 to 941, who held that all four accounts were partial and that the fourth, the reedfolk's Tide, was the one we had never seriously attempted to falsify. She was correct about the last part. She was scraped off the roll in 941 and her lectures were unsaid, which is a word we use here and which I will not soften for you: the Circle used its own craft to make a member quieter, and she is now a ghost under a line of ink, and every Sayer above the rank of Speaker knows it and we do not discuss it. — You asked what my account fails at. That is the other thing. It does not fail at Tessane. We did.

teach.speaker: Aldith Sulion
teach.text: Everyone asks and I say yes to about one in nine, so do not be flattered. — The first Binding, then: a short sentence about where you end. Forty marks, and before you make a face about it, the fee is the teaching. A saying somebody gave you for nothing sits in the mouth like a borrowed coat. You will say it back to me three times and you will pay for it and then it will be yours and I will not have to hear about it again.

choices.text: Forty marks. Say it and I'll say it back.
I don't have forty marks.
Another time.

teach_done.speaker: Aldith Sulion
teach_done.text: Again. — Again. — Good. It is a poor sentence and it will hold for about as long as it takes somebody to finish arguing with it, and that is usually long enough. Do not say it at a wall and expect to be impressed. Say it at something coming for you and then tell me it is a poor sentence.

teach_poor.speaker: Aldith Sulion
teach_poor.text: Then come back when you do. There is a binder on Lantern Row who sells the working in a book for a quarter of that, and it is a bad book, and you will learn it badly, and you will be alive, which is the argument in its favour. I have not told you this.

bye.speaker: Aldith Sulion
bye.text: Go. And speak up in the marsh; they are quiet there and you will fall into it within a week.

notes: Sayer of the Candle (WORLD_BIBLE 1.2). Merrowby-born; Tobin's cousin. Warm, gossipy, and the one who quietly tells the player they need not pay the Circle's price.

greetings.text: You told the Circle no. In the stairwell. Out loud. I have dined on that for a fortnight and I shall dine on it again.
There you are! I've been saying your name all week, which in my account is doing you a favour and in Sulion's is a breach of the acoustics.
Merrowby! You've come from Merrowby. Is Tobin still ringing that bell at a different hour to keep them all on their toes? He is. Of course he is.
People speak well of you, which is not a pleasantry, it is a measurement, and I take it more seriously than my colleagues take their instruments.
You gave the bell back to the water. Sulion has not said a word about it in eight days, which from Sulion is a howl of anguish.

greet.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
greet.text: Cresswell! Bennick. Sayer of the Candle, Merrowby-born, cousin to a man who keeps an inn inside a bell, which I mention in the first sentence to everyone I meet.

choices.text: Give me your account of the Dwindling.
The others say you are wrong.
What does your account fail at?
Is there another way to get what I need?
Why do you invent names for people?
Could you teach me a saying?
What do you know about Tessane?
I'll let you get on.

lecture.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
lecture.text: The world is a candle, the sun is its flame, and every hearth is a small copy of it. A flame goes out when nobody tends it. That's the whole lecture; the rest is examples and I have hundreds. — Tending is everything done with care and in company. Cooking. Mending. Naming children. Telling your neighbours about your other neighbours. Gossip is a kind of prayer, and I say that in this building where it gets me laughed at, and then I go down to the quay and the fishers tell me who has fallen out with whom and I am at my devotions. A person nobody speaks of goes quiet, and one day is not there. You have seen the Wardens' book. Every line in it is a place that stopped being talked about. That is not a symbol of my account. That is my account, in ink, kept by a militia who have never heard of me.

the_others.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
the_others.text: Sulion is right about the Builders and wrong about people, which is a common shape of error. Her bell is enormous and cold and explains every ruin in the basin and cannot explain a kitchen. Ask her why the warmest village in Hearthvale is the noisiest one, and she will tell you that is not sound in any sense she can measure, which is true, and which is her problem and not mine. — Ondrael I will not mock. Her account is the one that frightens me, because it is the only one in which nothing you do matters very much, and she is too good a scholar to soften it. When she is wrong she says so within the hour. I have known Sayers take a decade.

the_failure.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
the_failure.text: Oh, it fails, and it fails at the biggest objects in the world, which is embarrassing for a man who talks as much as I do. — The Builders' works. Cold, enormous, tended by nobody for a thousand years, and standing. The Seat has had no gossip, no hearth, no festivals, no children named after it. By my account it should have gone before Larkstead did. It has not gone and Larkstead has. I cannot get round it. I have tried the argument that the Cantor is himself the tending, one soul doing the work of a village, and Sulion demolished it in front of nineteen students in about four sentences, and she was right, and I bought her a drink.

the_quiet_word.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
the_quiet_word.text: There is, and I will be in trouble for saying so on the stair, so we are walking while I say it. — You do not need the Circle. You need an account of what the Toll is doing, and there are four of them in the world, and the Circle holds three and charges for the privilege of hearing them argue. The fourth is in the marsh, and the reedfolk will give it to you for nothing at all, if you are willing to sit down and wait a day or two for it. Go west. Ask for Tallissa Oul at Isseva. Sit down when she looks at you. Do not fill the silences; they are load-bearing.

the_names.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
the_names.text: Because a greeting with a name in it is a small fire and a greeting without one is a nod. If I don't know yours I'll make one up and use it cheerfully until you correct me, and the correcting is the point: you have now said your own name out loud to a stranger in a market, in front of the fish-woman and two clerks, and it is in the air, and that is four people's worth of tending that cost me the embarrassment of calling you Barnaby. I do about forty of those a day. It's the only magic I am any good at and it has no fee.

tessane.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
tessane.text: ...Right. Here is the part that costs me something to say, since you have the page in your hand and will get it out of Ondrael anyway. — The Circle unsaid her. Not exiled, not tried; unsaid. Her name scraped, her lectures withdrawn, her students told to attribute the useful parts to the Circle generally. Ninety-odd years of it. And the thing I cannot get past, as the man who stands up and says that speaking of people keeps them warm: it worked. There is a woman who was right about something and there is nothing left of her but a shadow under a line, and my account says that is exactly what should have happened, and I teach my account on Merrowday and I think about Tessane on the other six.

teach.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
teach.text: Yes. Now, before you've given me a reason, because the ones who have a reason ready have usually already needed it. — This one is the midwife's. Not a healing; an instruction, issued firmly, to the parts of a person that have become excitable. Say it like you are telling somebody's frightened aunt to sit down. Not unkindly. Just as though the sitting down were already agreed.

choices.text: Say it. I'll say it back three times.
Not now.

teach_done.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
teach_done.text: There. Free, and I want it noted that Sulion charges forty marks for hers and that I have never once said so in front of her. — It will not save anybody. It will buy you the quarter of an hour it takes to fetch somebody who can, and I have spent that quarter of an hour twice, and both times it was the whole of the difference. Go on. And if you use it on a stranger, tell me after. I collect those.

bye.speaker: Bennick Cresswell
bye.text: Off you go. And say somebody's name today who isn't expecting it. That's not a lecture. Well. It is, but it's a short one.

notes: Sayer of the Breath (WORLD_BIBLE 1.3), Oskel-blooded. Quiet, tired, honest. She times her own held breath to see whether it is getting shorter.

greetings.text: Shut the door. — Not like that. Quietly. Thank you.
You went into the singing shaft and came out. I have been reading about that shaft for twenty years from a chair.
The eighth verse. My mother's clan will have it by winter and my mother has been dead for nine years and I find I am not able to be scholarly about this yet.
You are very loud now. I mean that literally, in the technical sense, and I am not certain it is good for you.
It is the hour of the glass. Sit down; you can hold the sand for me and then I need not stop to turn it.

greet.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
greet.text: Ondrael. Sayer of the Breath. Speak at whatever volume you like; I read lips as well, from the mine years.

choices.text: Give me your account of the Dwindling.
The others say you are wrong.
What does your account fail at?
Why do you time your own breath?
I found a scraped line in the roll. Tessane.
You have clan blood.
Teach me a Hush.
Thank you.

lecture.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
lecture.text: Something vast breathed the world out and is now breathing in. What lies nearest the mouth goes first: the very old, the very deep, the forgotten. — I will give you the evidence rather than the poetry, because the poetry is my colleagues' department. The oldest places are failing first, in order, and the order holds across six regions and four cultures who do not talk to each other. Giants were breathed in long ago and their bones are still here, which is what is left when a thing is taken back but its weight is not; you may walk through a ribcage in Skerrow and I have, and it is not a metaphor and it is eleven yards high. The clans keep long memories because memory is a hand on the rope. That is not sentiment either. It is the only intervention anyone has ever demonstrated to work, and it works badly, and it is what we have.

the_others.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
the_others.text: Sulion is not wrong. That is the tiresome thing about Sulion. Sound behaves in the deep places exactly as she says it does, and if she would stop insisting that the bell is the whole of it she would be the best scholar in this building. — Cresswell is right about villages and wrong about scale, and he knows it, and he does it anyway because his account is the only one of the three that tells a person what to do on a Tuesday. I do not think that makes it true. I think it makes it useful, and I have started to wonder, lately, whether I know the difference as well as I did at thirty.

the_failure.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
the_failure.text: The Seat. — If something is breathing in, and it takes the oldest and deepest first, then the Cantor's Seat should have gone before the Choir, and the Choir before Greyfold, and Greyfold before Larkstead. Instead the Seat is the one thing in the basin that has not gone, and it is the oldest and deepest thing there is, and it is holding a note, and it has been holding it since before the Toll fell. My account has a hole in it in the exact shape of the largest object in the south. I put that in the first ten minutes of every lecture. Students find it alarming. It is alarming. I would rather they were alarmed by the right thing.

the_glass.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
the_glass.text: Because if the world is being breathed in, it is a reasonable hypothesis that breath itself is shortening, and nobody has ever taken the measurement. Forty-one years of an evening, a sand-glass, and my own lungs. — It is shorter. It is shorter by a little over what you would expect from a woman going from three to forty-four. Not much. Not enough to publish, and I have not published it, and I have been asked twice why not. Because I am the instrument, and the instrument is frightened, and a frightened instrument reads low. When I can get somebody young and unfrightened to sit and do it for forty years, we shall know something.

choices.text: I'll sit and hold the glass tonight.
That's a lonely piece of work.

the_glass_2.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
the_glass_2.text: ...Yes. All right. Yes. Ten to the hour, the small room, and you turn it when I nod and you do not speak, and you write the figure yourself in your own hand so that it is not mine. — Thank you. That is the first time anyone in this Circle has offered, and I have been in this Circle for twenty-two years, and Cresswell would say something about that and he would be right.

tessane.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
tessane.text: Tessane. Say it once more and then we will not say it on the stairs again. — She was a Sayer of the Tide, the reedfolk's account, which this Circle does not teach and did not want taught in Tollmere. Y.T. 941 they scraped her line and unsaid her lectures. I found the page eleven years ago doing something else entirely. — Here is what I want you to understand, and it is not a scandal, it is a result. We are an institution that holds that speaking a thing makes it more so. We applied our own craft to a colleague, deliberately, to make her less so. And it worked. That is the most successful experiment in the history of the Sayers' Circle and it is not written down anywhere, and the woman it was performed on is a ghost under a line of ink. — When you profess, in the hall, in front of them: you may say any of the three. Or you may say the fourth, and say her name, and there is nothing in the Circle's law that forbids it, because nobody ever imagined it would be needed.

the_clans.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
the_clans.text: My mother was Oskel. She came down to Tollmere at nineteen with a bone token and a mining cough and married a clerk, and she sang me the Rope-Song until I was old enough to be embarrassed by it, and then she stopped, and I would give a great deal to have those four years back. — There is a hole in that song where an eighth clan should be. That is not folklore; it is a gap in a structure that is otherwise regular, and the clans have kept it open for a thousand years by singing around it. A people who will hold a space open for a thousand years for a name nobody can remember are doing something that my whole profession has failed to do with instruments.

teach.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
teach.text: I can. I would rather you understood first what you are doing, because Hush is the only school where the working and the disease are the same shape. — You take the noise out of a thing. That is all. The cold is what is left over. I have spent forty-one years measuring something that is taking the noise out of the world, and I teach its method to students, and I have never once found the bottom of that, and I have stopped expecting to. Do you still want it?

choices.text: I still want it.
Let me think about that.

teach_done.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
teach_done.text: Good. Under the breath — it will not go if you push it, it is not that kind of saying. — And say it out loud somewhere warm afterwards. Anything. A name, the price of fish. I am not being poetic. I have watched three Hush students get very quiet over a winter and two of them came back.

teach_wait.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
teach_wait.text: That is the correct answer and nobody gives it. Come back when you have thought; I am here every evening with a sand-glass and no company.

bye.speaker: Ismay Ondrael
bye.text: Go carefully in the deep places. Sound dies sooner down there, and people do not notice it happening, and then they do not notice much.
